1 # Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour — proof of concept and handoff 2 3 This is the handoff document from the proof-of-concept session. It is written so a Claude Code CLI session can start planning and building visualisations for more cars without the original conversation. Read it top to bottom once. After that, §6 (models), §7 (photo overlay) and §11 (backlog) are the working sections. 4 5 **Suggested first prompt for the CLI session:** 6 > Read `TOUR-POC.md` and the two pages in `poc/`. Then plan the move to a GitHub Pages repo with shared modules (§9, §10), and propose the next three cars and their subsystems from §8. Don't write code until I approve the plan. 7 8 --- 9 10 ## 1. Goal and audience 11 12 - **Who:** a vehicle engineer guiding a small group of friends, all car people, through the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart. The engineer is the "technical guy" and explains mechanisms at the cars. 13 - **What:** at selected cars, a phone shows the mechanism *working*. Ideally it's placed over a photo of that same exhibit, so people can see where the part sits under the bodywork. 14 - **Format decided so far:** printed cards with a QR code, one static web page per stop, and no app to install. AR is optional and comes later. 15 - **Constraints:** 16 - It has to work on friends' iPhones in Safari. 17 - Mobile signal in the building may be patchy, so the pages should work offline after one visit. 18 - Exhibits rotate, so check which cars are on display before finalising stops. 19 20 ## 2. Decisions made and why 21 22 | Decision | Reason | 23 |---|---| 24 | Web pages + QR cards rather than a native AR app | Nothing to install. Works on any phone. Covers about 80 % of the effect for about 10 % of the effort. | 25 | No live AR registration onto the real car | Museum cars sit behind barriers, with reflective paint, dim light and crowds. ARKit object detection and Vuforia Model Targets are fragile there. | 26 | Fitted **museum photo overlay** instead | Gives the "X-ray of this exact car" effect reliably. It uses a public CC BY photo of the actual exhibit and a camera fitted to it (§7). | 27 | Mechanisms **simulated**, not keyframed | Suspension is solved from link lengths and driven by a quarter-car model. Engine and blower are kinematic. The numbers on screen (camber, toe, load, boost) are consistent and can be explained at the car. | 28 | Mechanisms built in code from hardpoints, not from downloaded CAD | Free CAD of the exact Mercedes parts mostly doesn't exist (§8). Simple rods, arms and rotors read better at phone size than dense CAD meshes. | 29 | three.js 0.128.0, plain `

1	# Source Document: Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart - Vehicle & Exhibit Database
2	
3	## Part 1: Comprehensive List of Displayed Cars (Highlights)
4	The Mercedes-Benz Museum spans nine floors and 16,500 square meters, housing a total of 160 vehicles and over 1,500 exhibits. While a complete manifest of all 160 vehicles is subject to rotation, the permanent exhibition is structured into 7 chronological "Legend Rooms" and 5 thematic "Collection Rooms". Below is the comprehensive list of the most prominent vehicles on display, organized by their respective exhibit areas:
5	
6	### Legend 1: Pioneers – The Invention of the Automobile (1886–1900)
7	*   **Daimler Single-Cylinder "Grandfather Clock" Engine (1884):** A structural sculpture of steel and brass that heralded modern mobility.
8	*   **Daimler Riding Carriage / Reitwagen (1885):** The world's first motorcycle.
9	*   **Benz Patent-Motorwagen (1886):** Recognized as the first functional car powered by a combustion engine.
10	*   **Daimler Motorboat "Marie" (1888):** A prominent early application of the combustion engine for water travel. 
11	*   **Benz Victoria (1893):** An early endurance vehicle that tackled a 939-kilometer journey.
12	*   **Benz Motor Velocipede (1894):** Regarded as the first large-scale production car.
13	*   **Daimler Motorised Business Vehicle (1899):** An early commercial truck capable of a 500 kg payload.
14	
15	### Legend 2 & 3: Birth of the Brand & Times of Change (1900–1945)
16	*   **Mercedes-Simplex 40 PS (1902):** Often referred to as the oldest Mercedes still in existence and the first automobile of the modern age.
17	*   **Milnes-Daimler Double-Decker Bus (1904):** An early transit vehicle used in London.
18	*   **Benz 200 PS "Lightning Benz" / "Blitzen Benz" (1909):** A massive 1,312 cu in displacement racer capable of 141 mph.
19	*   **Mercedes-Benz 27/170 Typ SSK (1928):** A legendary pre-war open-wheel sports car with an angled front grille.
20	*   **Mercedes-Benz 540 K Streamliner (1938):** A masterclass in pre-war aerodynamic aesthetics.
21	*   **Mercedes-Benz L6500 Pritschenwagen (1938):** A heavy-duty pre-war industrial cargo truck.
22	
23	### Legend 4 & 5: Post-war Miracle & Visionaries (1945–1982)
24	*   **Mercedes-Benz 300 SL "Gullwing" (1954):** The iconic dream car of the 1950s with upward-opening doors.
25	*   **Mercedes-Benz Rennwagen-Schnelltransporter "Blue Wonder" (1955):** A high-speed flat-bed transport truck for race cars.
26	*   **Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe (1955):** A brutally fast roadster built from race car mechanics.
27	*   **Mercedes-Benz 190 SL (1955):** A beautiful classic roadster.
28	*   **Mercedes-Benz 220 S "Tailfin" (1959):** Known for its North American-inspired rear directional wings.
29	*   **Mercedes-Benz 300 SEL 6.3 (1968):** The top-of-the-line luxury predecessor to the modern S-Class.
30	*   **Mercedes-Benz 230 G "Papamobil" (1980):** The iconic modified G-Wagen used by Pope John Paul II.
31	*   **Mercedes-Benz 500 SLC Rallyewagen (1980):** A rare long-distance rally racer.
32	
33	### Legend 6, Legend 7 & Collection Rooms
34	*   **Mercedes-Benz Vision R 320 CDI (2005):** A concept vehicle showcasing emission-free mobility ambitions.
35	*   **Mercedes-Maybach 6 Concept:** A modern, dramatic luxury showcase.
36	*   **Mercedes-Benz C 111-II:** An experimental concept car.
37	*   **Mercedes-Benz 1624 Car Transporter:** A massive multi-level commercial vehicle transporter positioned high up in Collection Room 2.
38	*   **Silver Arrows Racing Cars:** Found in Legend 7 on an expansive banked curve display, celebrating the brand's racing lineage.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Part 2: Vehicles Exhibited for "Close-Up" Inspection
43	The museum has a specifically curated "Close-up" series, which highlights specific exhibits that allow visitors to see mechanical elements, raw craftsmanship, and intricate detailing at close range. These exhibits are specifically designed to expose their inner workings:
44	
45	1.  **Daimler Riding Carriage (1885):** Visitors can view the exposed two simple control levers (a metal handle for mixture formation and a wooden knob for the block brake), the glow-tube ignition tank, and the leather drive belts.
46	2.  **Daimler 'Grandfather Clock' Engine (1884):** Displayed as a bare steel and brass sculpture so the vertical cylinder and round crankcase can be closely examined.
47	3.  **Benz Victoria (1893):** Positioned so the mechanical geometry of its early kingpin steering linkage can be seen.
48	4.  **Daimler Motorboat 'Marie' (1888):** Visitors can inspect the white-painted doors that discreetly concealed the single-cylinder engine from passengers.
49	5.  **Daimler Motorised Business Vehicle (1899):** The sieve-like front panel is exposed to show the tubular radiator designed by Wilhelm Maybach.
50	6.  **Mercedes-Benz 1624 Car Transporter:** Exhibited so the heavy-duty hydraulic control elements and the hybrid drive of the loading platforms (pulley blocks and hydraulics) can be inspected in high detail.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Part 3: Technical Highlights & Corresponding Cars (Worthy of Separate Discussion)
55	This structured list isolates the most important technical innovations present at the museum. It maps directly to specific vehicles and serves as an excellent foundation for a NotebookLM study guide, visual presentation, or isolated audio discussion.
56	
57	*   **First High-Speed Four-Stroke Engine**
58	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle/Exhibit:** Daimler "Grandfather Clock" Engine (1884)
59	    *   **Technical Details:** Developed in a garden house by Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach. Initially produced 1 hp (0.5 hp in the riding carriage) at a then-astounding 600 revolutions per minute.
60	*   **Kingpin Steering Innovation**
61	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Benz Victoria (1893)
62	    *   **Technical Details:** Replaced crude central-pivot steering systems, making cornering noticeably safer and allowing vehicles to comfortably navigate nearly 1,000 km journeys on primitive roads.
63	*   **Invention of the Tubular Radiator**
64	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Daimler Motorised Business Vehicle (1899)
65	    *   **Technical Details:** Created by Wilhelm Maybach to drastically improve engine cooling efficiency under loads, which enabled commercial vehicles to securely carry payloads up to 500 kg at 16 km/h.
66	*   **Supercharged Hillclimb Engineering**
67	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 27/170 Typ SSK (1928)
68	    *   **Technical Details:** Featured a massive 220-hp supercharged inline-six engine housed in a skinny, lightweight fuselage built specifically for dominance in uphill racing.
69	*   **Early Implementation of Modern Aerodynamics**
70	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 540 K Streamliner (1938)
71	    *   **Technical Details:** Despite featuring free-standing front mudguards, it utilized sweeping, wind-tunnel-tested curves to achieve a highly impressive drag coefficient (Cd) of just 0.36. 
72	*   **High-Torque Heavy Diesel Powertrain**
73	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz L6500 Pritschenwagen (1938)
74	    *   **Technical Details:** Equipped with a whopping 12.5-liter six-cylinder diesel engine positioned in front of the forward axle, enabling the transport of up to 14,000 pounds of payload.
75	*   **Bridging Race-Car Physics with Road-Car Usability**
76	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe (1955)
77	    *   **Technical Details:** Housed the mechanical chassis and a 3.0-liter inline-eight engine (310 hp) from a pure race car. Capable of an astonishing 180 mph in an era where most passenger cars struggled to hit 100 mph.
78	*   **High-Speed Commercial Aerodynamics**
79	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz Rennwagen-Schnelltransporter (1955)
80	    *   **Technical Details:** A heavy transport flat-bed utilizing a slippery aerodynamic profile and a 3.0-liter inline-six engine (approx. 200 hp), enabling a loaded truck to cruise on the Autobahn at 106 mph.
81	*   **Integrated Projectile Armor on a Passenger Chassis**
82	    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 230 G "Papamobil" (1980)
83	    *   **Technical Details:** A standard luxurious G-Wagen chassis that was heavily modified with golden adornments, a high-visibility seating cupola, and later retrofitted with comprehensive projectile protection in 1981.

# Plan: Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour on GitHub Pages

## Context
`museum-tour-poc/` has two working single-file PoC pages: the 190 E (five-link axle + M102) and the 540 K (wishbone front suspension + Roots blower). It also has a photo-fit tool and a handoff doc (`TOUR-POC.md`). `mercedes-museum-research.md` lists the museum's highlights. The pages are 42–55 KB monoliths that share about 70 % of their code and use three.js r128 globals, so each new car costs a lot of copy-paste and context.

**Goal:** a static GitHub Pages site where friends scan a QR code, walk the museum route and see each mechanism working, offline after one visit, on iPhone and iPad. It needs a modular layout where a new car is mostly one data file and a mechanism is a reusable module.

**Decided with you:**
- Native ES modules with a current, pinned three.js.
- Iteration 1 = migrate the **190 E** and **540 K**, and add four new interactive highlights: **Daimler "Grandfather Clock" engine (1884)**, **Benz Victoria double-pivot steering (1893)**, **300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé (straight-eight + desmodromic valves)** and the **SSK supercharger (1928)**.
- Playwright WebKit smoke tests on top of the Node model tests.

Repo facts: `abelkun-androniq/MercedesExperience` is **public**, so Pages is free. There's one commit (`ecdd37d`), and everything else is untracked. The root `540k-teaser.html`, `five-link-teaser.html` and `photo-*.jpg` are byte-identical to the `museum-tour-poc/poc/` copies. Node is v26. No iOS Simulator runtimes are installed.

## Key decisions
| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Build | **No bundler.** Native ES modules plus an import map in `stop.html`. A Node-only `tools/build.mjs` runs at deploy (stamps the SW). |
| three.js | Vendored, exact pinned version (newest stable at implementation time) through `tools/vendor-three.mjs <ver>`. That script also copies the needed addons (OrbitControls; GLTFLoader when needed). Upgrading = rerun it + run the tests. |
| URLs | One shell `stop.html?s=<slug>` for every stop, so QR codes stay stable when a stop is upgraded. `s` is validated against the tour list before any dynamic import. |
| Data vs code | `stops/<slug>/car.js` is **pure data** (no three.js), so Node tests and the index can import every car cheaply. Subsystems are referenced by id string. |
| Fonts | Drop Google Fonts and use the system font stacks already in the PoC CSS. No third-party requests, and nothing extra to cache offline. |
| Offline | Service worker, cache-first, precaching **every** stop. Friends often scan once at the entrance and then have no signal. The cache version is a content hash, stamped by the build. |
| Hosting | GitHub Actions: unit tests → Playwright → build → deploy Pages artifact. |
| iOS floor | iOS 16.4+ (import maps). Older devices see a clear "update iOS" message. |

The search didn't turn up the bore and stroke for the 1885 Grandfather Clock engine, and I found no direct displacement figure for it. The sources do agree on the core specs and the ignition system, with a few conflicts.

- **Power and speed:** One source gives about 1 hp at 600 rpm for the first version, and calls those figures sensational for the time. In its first version, this power unit produced 0.74 kW (1 hp) at 600 rpm. Another lists 600 rpm as the speed, versus roughly 120 to 180 rpm for most engines of the era. a speed of 600 rpm, when at the time most engines could only achieve about 120 to 180 rpm.
- **Configuration:** The engine was a single vertical cylinder, air-cooled, with a large cast-iron flywheel. single vertical cylinder; air cooling; large cast-iron flywheel
- **Ignition:** Hot-tube ignition was covered by patent DRP 28022, which describes an "uncooled, heat-insulated engine with unregulated hot-tube ignition". The patent date is commonly given as April 3, 1885. Gottlieb Daimler patented his "grandfather clock" engine on this date in 1885.
- **Displacement (not confirmed for this engine):** A 264 cm³ single-cylinder engine is listed at 0.5 hp at 600 rpm. The single-cylinder engine with 264 cm³ displacement had an output of 0.5 hp at 600 rpm. A different source gives 0.5 hp at 700 rpm for the 1885 riding car that used a scaled-down version of the engine. In 1885, Daimler and Maybach fitted a scaled-down version of the Grandfather Clock into a wooden two-wheeler, the so-called riding car. In this car, the engine developed 0.5 hp (0.37 kW) at 700 rpm. The 264 cm³ figure may belong to a different or later unit, so treat it as unverified for the original.

Sources that would settle the bore, stroke, and displacement include Daimler's patent text and museum or Mercedes-Benz archive specifications for the original engine. A follow-up search aimed at those would be the next step.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The user wants a GitHub Pages webpage for a technical museum tour of the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart.
   - It should be based on the folder contents, especially the research doc of museum highlights (`museum-tour-poc/mercedes-museum-research.md`) and the PoC handoff (`museum-tour-poc/TOUR-POC.md` plus two PoC pages).
   - Priorities: token efficiency, a modular architecture, easy extendability and upgradability (more detailed models later, more cars), and testing and use on both iPhones and iPads.
   - First step was a plan in plan mode. The plan was approved and implementation is underway.
   - User decisions:
     - Native ES modules with a current three.js.
     - First iteration: migrate the existing 190 E and 540 K, and add new interactive highlights. The user's words: "I want the highlights to be interactive if possible. Lets not do all of them on the first round, migrate the existing ones and add 3 more from the higlights to start with for the first iteration." The user then picked **all four** offered: Grandfather Clock engine, Benz Victoria steering, 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé, SSK supercharger.
     - Testing: Playwright WebKit smoke tests (iPhone/iPad emulation) plus Node unit tests plus a manual real-device checklist.
   - Constraints:
     - I said I'd ask before each commit/push.
     - Don't move or delete anything in `museum-tour-poc/` until the user approves a baseline commit of the PoC. Build the new structure alongside it.
     - The root duplicates (`540k-teaser.html`, `five-link-teaser.html`, `photo-190e.jpg`, `photo-540k.jpg`) are byte-identical to the `poc/` copies and are to be deleted (Phase 0).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Static site with no bundler: native ES modules plus an import map in `stop.html` (iOS 16.4+, feature-detected with `HTMLScriptElement.supports("importmap")`).
   - three.js 0.186.1 vendored by `tools/vendor-three.mjs`. `three.module.min.js` imports `./three.core.js`, which is rewritten to `./three.core.min.js`. OrbitControls comes from `three/addons/`.
   - Physically based lights: PoC intensities × π. `outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace`. Colours come from CSS tokens via `stage.bind(color, token)`.
   - One shell page `stop.html?s=<slug>`, with the slug validated against `stops/tour.js` before any dynamic import. Stable QR URLs.
   - `stops/<slug>/car.js` is pure data (Node-importable). Subsystems are referenced by id string and loaded with `import("../../subsystems/${id}.js")`; the id is checked against `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/`.
   - Subsystem contract: `create(ctx, params)`.
     - `ctx = { stage, carRoot, frame, ride, panel, reducedMotion }`.
     - Returns `{ layout({active, onPhoto}), update(dt, {onPhoto}) }`.
   - The shell owns: switches, photo view, outline toggle, ghost body, loop. Each frame it resets the carRoot pose before calling the active component's `update`.
   - Declarative panel widgets (`lib/app/panel.js`).
   - Models (TOUR-POC §6):
     - Multi-link closure: Newton–Raphson with Rodrigues rotation.
     - Quarter-car: semi-implicit Euler, dt 0.0005, road loop of 24 m, SLOWMO 0.2.
     - Slider-crank generalised to N cylinders from the firing order: interval 4π/N; offset[cyl] = k·interval; throw = −k·interval mod 2π.
     - Roots blower: first-order lag.
     - Desmo/spring valve: simulated in cam-angle steps at true rpm; spring rate derived from `floatRpm`.
     - Double-pivot trapezoid steering: analytic circle–circle closure, β = atan(k/wb); centre-pivot comparison.
   - Service worker:
     - Cache-first.
     - `tools/build.mjs` (to be written) stamps VERSION (content hash) and FILES into `_site/sw.js`.
     - `ignoreSearch` for pages.
     - Status reported over a MessageChannel.
     - Skipped on localhost/LAN unless `?sw=1`; any earlier registration is unregistered there.
   - Deploy: GitHub Actions running unit tests → Playwright (macos-latest planned, for WebKit WebGL) → build → `upload-pages-artifact` → `deploy-pages`. Manual step for the user: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
   - Token efficiency:
     - `CLAUDE.md` of 80 lines or fewer.
     - `.claude/settings.json` denying Read on `vendor/**`, `_site/**`, `node_modules/**`, `test-results/**`.
     - Small files.
   - Conventions: mm, x forward, y left, z up; camber negative = top inboard; toe positive = in; travel positive = bump; scene units are metres.
   - Note: Read tool output on the PoC files got elided by a "caveman" hook. Use Bash `sed -n` or `mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve` to get full code.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **Plan:** `/Users/kunabel/.claude/plans/i-want-to-make-misty-starfish.md` (approved). Phases:
     - 0: baseline commit.
     - 1: foundation + parity.
     - 2: offline/PWA/CI.
     - 3: four new stops — SSK, Daimler engine, 300 SLR, Victoria.
     - 4: device pass + accuracy.
   - **`lib/model/linkage.js`:** exports `rotm`, `mul`, `gauss`, and `createLinkage({W0, links, wheelR})`, which returns `{W0, links (with cl, len2), carrierPoint(q, local, R), residual(q, s), solve(q0, s), angles(q) → {camber, toe, track}}`.
   - **`lib/model/quarter-car.js`:** exports `ROAD_PERIOD = 24`, `roadProfile(s)`, `createCorner(p)` (corner has `step(zr, dt)` and `fStatic`), and `createRide({ride, xFront, xRear, speed = 25/3.6, dt = 0.0005})`. The ride has `{front, rear, dist, t, step(h), corner(axle), travelMm(axle), loadPct(axle), bodyZ(), pitch()}`; `pitch = −asin((front.zs − rear.zs)/wb)`.
   - **`lib/model/engine.js`:** exports:
     - `STROKES = ["Power", "Exhaust", "Intake", "Compression"]`;
     - `pistonPos`;

The search turned up consistent core data for the 1885 "Standuhr" engine, but the power figures vary by source.

- **Bore, stroke, displacement:** One data sheet gives 58 × 100 mm and 264 cc for a single-cylinder engine Bohrung x Hub 58 x 100 mm, Hubraum 264 ccm.
- **Power and speed:** Sources disagree. One lists 0,5 PS bei 600 U/min. Another gives 0,37 kW bei 650/min, and a third cites 0,37 kW (0,5 PS) bei 700/min. A fourth says the first version delivers 0,74 kW (1 PS) bei 600/min.
- **Ignition:** The engine used hot-tube ignition. One source notes that in favor of a hot tube system invented by Leo Funk, since Daimler also distrusted electricity. Another credits the Glührohrzündung und der Kurvennutensteuerung for the engine's output.
- **Context:** The engine was built into the Reitwagen, which was ein technisches Versuchsträgerfahrzeug and not a production model. The Standuhr name also applies to a later 462 cc, 1.1 PS variant with a 70 × 120 mm bore and stroke Bohrung: 70 mm Hub: 120 mm Gesamthubraum: 462 ccm, so the two should not be confused.

The 0.5 PS / 600 rpm figure is the most widely repeated for the 1885 Reitwagen engine. The 0.37 kW figure and the 1 PS version are less consistent with it, so I would treat the exact rated speed as uncertain unless checked against a primary source such as Mercedes-Benz Classic archive material.

# Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour

Static GitHub Pages site: one page per exhibit showing its mechanism working (three.js), offline after one visit, for
iPhone/iPad Safari (iOS 16.4+, import maps). No bundler: native ES modules; `tools/build.mjs` only stamps the service worker.

## Map
- `index.html` route (lib/app/index.js) · `stop.html?s=<slug>` shell for every stop (lib/app/shell.js) · `sw.js` offline cache
- `stops/tour.js` route order, room, level: single source for order and prev/next · `stops/<slug>/car.js` pure data (+ photo.jpg)
- `lib/model/` pure maths, Node-tested: linkage (multi-link closure), quarter-car (ride), engine (N-cylinder slider-crank,
  timing), blower, valvetrain (spring float, desmo), steering (double-pivot trapezoid, centre pivot)
- `lib/scene/` stage (renderer, cameras, lights, theme tokens, loop), helpers, ghost-body, road
- `lib/app/` shell, panel (declarative widgets, API in its header), offline, index, theme.css
- `subsystems/<id>.js` one mechanism each: linkage-suspension, inline-engine, roots-blower, desmo-valvetrain, steering
- `tools/` build, vendor-three, fit-photo-camera (+ photo-fits/*.json) · `docs/TOUR-POC.md` (model maths §6), `docs/research.md`
- `vendor/three/` is generated by `npm run vendor -- <version>`: never read or edit it.

## Conventions
- Vehicle frame: mm in configs, metres in the scene; x forward, y left, z up; origin per car in `frame.origin`.
- Camber − = top inboard · toe + = toe-in · travel + = bump · steer + = left.
- Colours only through CSS tokens (`stage.bind`, `stage.tokenMat`, `var(--…)` in SVG): never hard-code theme colours.
- Illustrative numbers get a comment in car.js and a line in `unverified` (the page shows it). Sources go in `sources`.
- Panel DOM is built with textContent only; widget ids must be unique within a component.

## Contracts
- car.js: `{ slug, title, name, year, summary, eyebrow, lede, frame?, ride?, orbit?, sun?, body?: { ghost }, photo?,
  components: [{ id, label, subsystem, view: { pos, target }, ghost?: { fill, edge }, params, talk }], note, unverified, sources }`
- Subsystem: `export function create(ctx, params)` with ctx `{ stage, carRoot, frame, ride, panel, reducedMotion }`, returns
  `{ layout({ active, onPhoto }), update(dt, { onPhoto }) }`. The shell owns switches, photo view, outline, ghost body and
  the loop, and resets carRoot's pose each frame before calling the active component's `update`.

## Recipes
- Add a stop: entry in `stops/tour.js` + `stops/<slug>/car.js` (copy the closest sibling). Optional photo: 1200 px wide, CC
  licence with credit, camera fitted with `node tools/fit-photo-camera.mjs tools/photo-fits/<slug>.json`. Tests find it via tour.js.
- Add a mechanism: `lib/model/<x>.js` + `tests/unit/<x>.test.mjs` first, then `subsystems/<x>.js`.
- Upgrade three.js: `npm run vendor -- <version>` (a release at least two weeks old), then `npm test && npm run e2e`.

## Commands
- `npm test` unit tests (models + configs) · `npm run e2e` Playwright: WebKit iPhone/iPad × 4 and Chromium offline (builds first)
- `npm run serve` dev server on :8765 (service worker off on localhost unless `?sw=1`) · `?debug` exposes `window.__tour`
- `npm run build` → `_site/` · deploy: push to main; `.github/workflows/pages.yml` tests, then deploys.

## Real-device checklist (iPhone and iPad Safari, from the Pages URL)
Portrait and landscape · light and dark · orbit, pinch, sliders · photo overlay lines up with Car outline on · airplane mode
after one visit: index → every stop · Add to Home Screen, launch offline · iPad Split View · Low Power Mode still animates at
true speed · Web Inspector over USB shows no errors. LAN (`http://<mac-ip>:8765`) checks layout only: service workers need HTTPS.

## Open
- Confirm on site: rooms and levels in tour.js; which 540 K is shown (Cabriolet B photo vs the 1938 Streamliner in the research).
- `museum-tour-poc/` is the original PoC, kept until the baseline commit; remove afterwards (history stays in git).
EOF

I've built all six stops and the full test, build and deploy setup, and all tests pass. Nothing is committed or pushed yet; that's waiting on you (questions at the end).

**The route** (walking order, top floor down):

| Stop | What you can do with it |
|---|---|
| Grandfather Clock engine | Single cylinder with flywheels in the crankcase, hot-tube ignition, an intake valve sucked open by the piston, and a real-rpm readout |
| Benz Victoria | Top-down steering with a slider. Switch between double-pivot and centre-pivot and watch where the wheel axes meet: inner/outer/ideal angles, axis miss, turning circle, front support width |
| SSK | The 540 K supercharger module reused with six cylinders, plus the six-cylinder engine, firing order 1-5-3-6-2-4 |
| 540 K, 190 E | Migrated from the PoC; the model maths gives exactly the PoC's numbers |
| 300 SLR Uhlenhaut | Straight-eight with direct-injection spray. A desmo close-up puts a desmo valve beside a spring valve on the same cam: raise the rpm and the spring valve floats off the cam while the desmo valve keeps following it |

**Tests**
- 39 unit tests pass: models plus a check that every stop is wired up correctly.
- 33 browser tests pass: every stop on iPhone and iPad, portrait and landscape, in Safari's engine, plus an offline test. They check that each stop renders, every switch works, the readouts move, there's no horizontal scroll and no console errors.
- After one visit the whole tour (39 files, 1.3 MB) is stored, and a different stop then opens in airplane mode.
- Side by side with the PoC, the 190 E looks the same after the three.js upgrade. The only difference is the road, now neutral grey instead of slightly blue.

**Facts to settle before friends see it** (each page lists its own in an "Illustrative, not verified" note):
- **Grandfather Clock:** sources disagree on power (0.5–1 hp at about 600 rpm) and on whether 58 × 100 mm describes this engine or the Riding Car's version. The research doc says 1884; most sources date the patent to 1885.
- **Research doc corrections:** the Victoria has double-pivot steering, not "kingpin" steering, and the 300 SLR exhibit is a coupé, not a roadster.
- **300 SLR:** I couldn't confirm the M196's firing order, so the page uses a generic straight-eight order. The 33° engine lean comes from one source.
- **Victoria:** I found no published dimensions, so all of its geometry is a plausible guess.
- **All stops:** rooms and levels need checking on site, and so does which 540 K is on display.

The four new stops are 3D only for now. Each gets a "Museum photo" view once a CC-licensed photo is found and its camera is fitted.

**You'll need to do:**
- GitHub → Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions** (one time).
- Run the real-device checklist in `CLAUDE.md` once it's live.

2. A commit with the new site.

result.output:
# Source Document: Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart - Vehicle & Exhibit Database

## Part 1: Comprehensive List of Displayed Cars (Highlights)
The Mercedes-Benz Museum spans nine floors and 16,500 square meters, housing a total of 160 vehicles and over 1,500 exhibits. While a complete manifest of all 160 vehicles is subject to rotation, the permanent exhibition is structured into 7 chronological "Legend Rooms" and 5 thematic "Collection Rooms". Below is the comprehensive list of the most prominent vehicles on display, organized by their respective exhibit areas:

### Legend 1: Pioneers – The Invention of the Automobile (1886–1900)
*   **Daimler Single-Cylinder "Grandfather Clock" Engine (1884):** A structural sculpture of steel and brass that heralded modern mobility.
*   **Daimler Riding Carriage / Reitwagen (1885):** The world's first motorcycle.
*   **Benz Patent-Motorwagen (1886):** Recognized as the first functional car powered by a combustion engine.
*   **Daimler Motorboat "Marie" (1888):** A prominent early application of the combustion engine for water travel. 
*   **Benz Victoria (1893):** An early endurance vehicle that tackled a 939-kilometer journey.
*   **Benz Motor Velocipede (1894):** Regarded as the first large-scale production car.
*   **Daimler Motorised Business Vehicle (1899):** An early commercial truck capable of a 500 kg payload.

### Legend 2 & 3: Birth of the Brand & Times of Change (1900–1945)
*   **Mercedes-Simplex 40 PS (1902):** Often referred to as the oldest Mercedes still in existence and the first automobile of the modern age.
*   **Milnes-Daimler Double-Decker Bus (1904):** An early transit vehicle used in London.
*   **Benz 200 PS "Lightning Benz" / "Blitzen Benz" (1909):** A massive 1,312 cu in displacement racer capable of 141 mph.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 27/170 Typ SSK (1928):** A legendary pre-war open-wheel sports car with an angled front grille.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 540 K Streamliner (1938):** A masterclass in pre-war aerodynamic aesthetics.
*   **Mercedes-Benz L6500 Pritschenwagen (1938):** A heavy-duty pre-war industrial cargo truck.

### Legend 4 & 5: Post-war Miracle & Visionaries (1945–1982)
*   **Mercedes-Benz 300 SL "Gullwing" (1954):** The iconic dream car of the 1950s with upward-opening doors.
*   **Mercedes-Benz Rennwagen-Schnelltransporter "Blue Wonder" (1955):** A high-speed flat-bed transport truck for race cars.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe (1955):** A brutally fast roadster built from race car mechanics.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 190 SL (1955):** A beautiful classic roadster.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 220 S "Tailfin" (1959):** Known for its North American-inspired rear directional wings.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 300 SEL 6.3 (1968):** The top-of-the-line luxury predecessor to the modern S-Class.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 230 G "Papamobil" (1980):** The iconic modified G-Wagen used by Pope John Paul II.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 500 SLC Rallyewagen (1980):** A rare long-distance rally racer.

### Legend 6, Legend 7 & Collection Rooms
*   **Mercedes-Benz Vision R 320 CDI (2005):** A concept vehicle showcasing emission-free mobility ambitions.
*   **Mercedes-Maybach 6 Concept:** A modern, dramatic luxury showcase.
*   **Mercedes-Benz C 111-II:** An experimental concept car.
*   **Mercedes-Benz 1624 Car Transporter:** A massive multi-level commercial vehicle transporter positioned high up in Collection Room 2.
*   **Silver Arrows Racing Cars:** Found in Legend 7 on an expansive banked curve display, celebrating the brand's racing lineage.

---

## Part 2: Vehicles Exhibited for "Close-Up" Inspection
The museum has a specifically curated "Close-up" series, which highlights specific exhibits that allow visitors to see mechanical elements, raw craftsmanship, and intricate detailing at close range. These exhibits are specifically designed to expose their inner workings:

1.  **Daimler Riding Carriage (1885):** Visitors can view the exposed two simple control levers (a metal handle for mixture formation and a wooden knob for the block brake), the glow-tube ignition tank, and the leather drive belts.
2.  **Daimler 'Grandfather Clock' Engine (1884):** Displayed as a bare steel and brass sculpture so the vertical cylinder and round crankcase can be closely examined.
3.  **Benz Victoria (1893):** Positioned so the mechanical geometry of its early kingpin steering linkage can be seen.
4.  **Daimler Motorboat 'Marie' (1888):** Visitors can inspect the white-painted doors that discreetly concealed the single-cylinder engine from passengers.
5.  **Daimler Motorised Business Vehicle (1899):** The sieve-like front panel is exposed to show the tubular radiator designed by Wilhelm Maybach.
6.  **Mercedes-Benz 1624 Car Transporter:** Exhibited so the heavy-duty hydraulic control elements and the hybrid drive of the loading platforms (pulley blocks and hydraulics) can be inspected in high detail.

---

## Part 3: Technical Highlights & Corresponding Cars (Worthy of Separate Discussion)
This structured list isolates the most important technical innovations present at the museum. It maps directly to specific vehicles and serves as an excellent foundation for a NotebookLM study guide, visual presentation, or isolated audio discussion.

*   **First High-Speed Four-Stroke Engine**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle/Exhibit:** Daimler "Grandfather Clock" Engine (1884)
    *   **Technical Details:** Developed in a garden house by Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach. Initially produced 1 hp (0.5 hp in the riding carriage) at a then-astounding 600 revolutions per minute.
*   **Kingpin Steering Innovation**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Benz Victoria (1893)
    *   **Technical Details:** Replaced crude central-pivot steering systems, making cornering noticeably safer and allowing vehicles to comfortably navigate nearly 1,000 km journeys on primitive roads.
*   **Invention of the Tubular Radiator**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Daimler Motorised Business Vehicle (1899)
    *   **Technical Details:** Created by Wilhelm Maybach to drastically improve engine cooling efficiency under loads, which enabled commercial vehicles to securely carry payloads up to 500 kg at 16 km/h.
*   **Supercharged Hillclimb Engineering**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 27/170 Typ SSK (1928)
    *   **Technical Details:** Featured a massive 220-hp supercharged inline-six engine housed in a skinny, lightweight fuselage built specifically for dominance in uphill racing.
*   **Early Implementation of Modern Aerodynamics**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 540 K Streamliner (1938)
    *   **Technical Details:** Despite featuring free-standing front mudguards, it utilized sweeping, wind-tunnel-tested curves to achieve a highly impressive drag coefficient (Cd) of just 0.36. 
*   **High-Torque Heavy Diesel Powertrain**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz L6500 Pritschenwagen (1938)
    *   **Technical Details:** Equipped with a whopping 12.5-liter six-cylinder diesel engine positioned in front of the forward axle, enabling the transport of up to 14,000 pounds of payload.
*   **Bridging Race-Car Physics with Road-Car Usability**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe (1955)
    *   **Technical Details:** Housed the mechanical chassis and a 3.0-liter inline-eight engine (310 hp) from a pure race car. Capable of an astonishing 180 mph in an era where most passenger cars struggled to hit 100 mph.
*   **High-Speed Commercial Aerodynamics**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz Rennwagen-Schnelltransporter (1955)
    *   **Technical Details:** A heavy transport flat-bed utilizing a slippery aerodynamic profile and a 3.0-liter inline-six engine (approx. 200 hp), enabling a loaded truck to cruise on the Autobahn at 106 mph.
*   **Integrated Projectile Armor on a Passenger Chassis**
    *   **Corresponding Vehicle:** Mercedes-Benz 230 G "Papamobil" (1980)
    *   **Technical Details:** A standard luxurious G-Wagen chassis that was heavily modified with golden adornments, a high-visibility seating cupola, and later retrofitted with comprehensive projectile protection in 1981.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**
   - **Original request:** a GitHub Pages webpage for a technical museum tour of the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart. It is based on the research doc of highlights and the PoC handoff. Priorities: token efficiency, a modular architecture, easy extendability and upgradability (more detailed models, more cars), and testing and use on iPhone and iPad.
   - **Decisions made earlier:**
     - Native ES modules with three.js 0.186.1.
     - Iteration 1: migrate the 190 E and 540 K, plus four interactive highlights: Grandfather Clock engine, Benz Victoria steering, 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé, SSK supercharger.
     - Testing: Playwright WebKit smoke tests, Node unit tests, and a manual device checklist.
   - **Constraints:** ask before commits and pushes. The PoC folder was kept until the baseline commit; that is now done and the folder has been removed.
   - **This session:**
     - The user approved "yes, do all four and push" (baseline commit, site commit, PoC removal, push). Done.
     - The user said "you enable it and redeploy" (GitHub Pages). Done.
     - **Current request:** "Good! Add 10 more cars - whichever you think is best."

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Static site, no bundler.**
     - Import map in `stop.html`, iOS 16.4+.
     - three.js 0.186.1 vendored in `vendor/three/`, which agents must never read.
     - One shell page `stop.html?s=<slug>`. The slug is validated against `stops/tour.js` before any dynamic import.
   - **Cars and subsystems.**
     - `stops/<slug>/car.js` is pure data.
     - Subsystems are loaded with `import("../../subsystems/${id}.js")`; ids must match `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/`.
   - **Subsystem contract:** `create(ctx, params)`.
     - `ctx = { stage, carRoot, frame, ride, panel, reducedMotion }`.
     - Returns `{ layout({active, onPhoto}), update(dt, {onPhoto}) }`.
     - The shell owns switches, photo view, outline, ghost body and the loop. It resets the carRoot pose each frame before `update`.
   - **Panel widgets** (`lib/app/panel.js`):
     - Widget types: `readouts`, `trace`, `buttons` (`toggle: [on, off]`, or radio style with `pressed` and no `toggle`), `slider`, `meter`, `cells`, `legend`, `key`, `svg`, `text`, `list`.
     - A card can have a `badge`.
     - Widget ids must be unique within a component. Handles: `ui.set(id, text)`, `ui.toggle(id).set(bool)`, `ui.slider(id).set(v)`, `ui.meter(id).set(f, hot)`, `ui.cells(id).set(i, text, on)`, `ui.badge(id).set(text, on)`, `ui.el(id)`.
   - **Colours** only through CSS tokens: `stage.bind(color, token)`, `stage.tokenMat(token)`, `var(--…)`. Tokens: `--l1` orange/red, `--l2` yellow, `--l3` green (fuel), `--l4` blue, `--metal`, `--accent` teal, `--muted`, `--fg`, `--rule`, `--stage`.
   - **Conventions:**
     - mm in configs, metres in the scene; x forward, y left, z up.
     - Camber − = top inboard, toe + = in, travel + = bump, steer + = left.
     - Illustrative values get a comment plus an entry in `unverified`.
   - **Service worker:** cache-first. `tools/build.mjs` stamps VERSION (sha256, 12 hex) and FILES (`"./"` plus every file) into `_site/sw.js`. It is skipped on localhost unless `?sw=1`.
   - **CI** (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`):
     - Test job on macos-latest: `npm ci`, `npm test`, `playwright install webkit chromium`, `npm run e2e`.
     - Deploy job on ubuntu: `build`, `configure-pages@v5`, `upload-pages-artifact@v4`, `deploy-pages@v4`.
     - Concurrency group `pages-${{ github.ref }}`; cancel-in-progress only for PRs.
   - **Live site:** https://abelkun-androniq.github.io/MercedesExperience/ (Pages build_type: workflow, enabled via the gh API).
   - **Read tool caveat:** the caveman hook may elide Read output on large files. Use `sed -n` via Bash, or `mcp__caveman__caveman_retrieve`.
   - **Git hook:** "Entire" is enabled and pushes checkpoint refs automatically. Do not run entire setup or destructive commands without asking.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**
   - **`subsystems/roots-blower.js` (new)**
     - Params: `blower` (lib/model/blower.js), `order` (its length is the cylinder count), `engineLabel`, `offset?` (default `[0, 0, 0.12]`), `spacing?` (default 0.112).
     - Geometry: `BL = { x0: -0.02, x1: -0.2, zc: 0.24, d: 0.1, rc: 0.08, crankZ: 0, blockX0: -0.3 }`, with `blockX1 = blockX0 - (0.136 + (n-1)*sp)`.
     - Contents: rotors via the UVW matrix, figure-of-eight casing, crank throws from `layout(order).throwA`, clutch plates, gears, bore rings, air-path particles (220), flap hinge.
     - Panel: "Accelerator" card with a clutch badge and these widgets:
       - slider `throttle`;
       - readouts `pedal`, `rotor`, `boost`, `power`;
       - meter `boostMeter`;
       - buttons `auto` (toggle) and `floor`;
       - a key.
     - Second card "End view of the rotors": SVG with viewBox `-140 -95 280 190`.
   - **`subsystems/desmo-valvetrain.js` (new)**
     - Params: `cam {lift, open, duration, mass, preload, floatRpm, base}`, `rpm {min, max, value}` (crank rpm), `label`, `origin?`.
     - Constants: `SHOWN_REV_S 0.3`, `CAM_Z 0.12`, `STEM 0.1`.
     - Geometry:
       - Y positions: desmo valve `Yd = 0.05`, spring valve `Ys = -0.05`, closing cam `Yc = 0.1`.
       - Cam discs rotate about y with `rotation.y = phi`.
       - Equal-arm closing rocker: `zB = CAM_Z - base - lift - L`, `zA = CAM_Z - (base + lift - L)`.
       - The coil is built once and scaled with `coil.scale.z`.
       - `pose()` returns `{L, x}`.
     - Panel:
       - badge `state`: "Spring valve floating" / "Both valves on the cam";
       - slider `rpm` (step 100); changing it re-runs `simulateSpringValve`;
       - readouts `rpm`, `float`, `desmo`, `spring`;
       - SVG `lift` (viewBox `0 0 280 120`) with cam (dashed), desmo and spring polylines plus a cursor line;
       - a key;
       - play toggle;

The search confirms the basic layout of the Benz Patent-Motorwagen drivetrain, with a few points worth noting:

- **Engine and flywheel:** Benz placed the large flywheel horizontally to avoid gyroscopic effects that could hurt steering in tight bends. A bevel crown wheel at the upper end of the crankshaft links the drive components via a side shaft.
- **Belt and differential:** A flat belt ran from the engine to a countershaft. The countershaft had one speed, a fixed drive disc with an integrated differential, and an adjacent idler disc, so there was no multi-speed transmission and no reverse gear. The idler disc let the belt also act as a clutch.
- **Chains to the rear wheels:** A chain on each side ran from the countershaft to the rear wheels, which were fixed to the frame by a rigid axle and fully elliptic springs. Sources differ on the drive details. One source describes the rear wheels as driven by two side chains from the countershaft, while another says the engine spins the wheels through a differential, a leather belt, and a series of metal chains.
- **Later change:** Wikipedia notes that in order to accommodate the extra belt system for the low gear, the flywheel in Model 3 was changed from horizontal to vertical. So the horizontal flywheel and bevel-driven layout describe the original 1886 design, not later models.

The sources are mostly manufacturer and enthusiast pages, and one is a Wikipedia mirror, so the wording and details vary somewhat between them.

The search confirms most of the core details, but it doesn't give the compression ratio, and the sources disagree on engine speed and displacement.

- **Launch and firsts:** The 260 D (W 138) was shown at the Berlin motorcycle and automobile exhibition in February 1936, and series production commenced at the end of 1935. Sources generally describe it as the first series-production diesel passenger car. One source instead calls it one of the first two diesel engined series produced passenger cars, alongside the Hanomag Rekord diesel.
- **Engine:** The OM 138 is a straight-4 with a displacement of 2,545 cc, and it was the first diesel engine especially developed and made for a passenger car.
- **Pre-chamber and injection:** One source says the engine used the Mercedes-Benz pre-chamber system and Bosch injection pump.
- **Power and speed:** Wikipedia gives a rated power of 33 kW (45 PS; 44 hp) and a rated speed of 3000 rpm for the car engine. CarAdvice gives the same power but at 3200 rpm, so the speed figure conflicts.
- **Displacement conflict:** Autoblog describes the engine as a 2.4-liter I-4 engine, which contradicts the 2,545 cc figure above.
- **Compression ratio:** I found no source for it, so it remains unverified.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**
   - **Current request:** "Good! Add 10 more cars - whichever you think is best." Follow the existing architecture:
     - a `stops/tour.js` entry plus `stops/<slug>/car.js` for each car;
     - new `lib/model/*.js` with unit tests, then `subsystems/*.js`;
     - sourced facts; illustrative values commented and listed in `unverified`;
     - unit and e2e tests passing.
   - **Earlier in the project (done):** a static GitHub Pages site for a Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour.
     - Priorities: token efficiency, modularity, extensibility, iPhone/iPad.
     - Live at https://abelkun-androniq.github.io/MercedesExperience/.
   - **Standing constraint:** ask before commits and pushes. The previous approval ("yes, do all four and push") covered only those specific commits.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Stack:** no bundler; native ES modules with an import map; three.js 0.186.1 vendored in `vendor/three/` (never read it).
   - **Shell:** `stop.html?s=<slug>` validated against tour.js.
   - **Subsystem contract:** `create(ctx, params)` with `ctx = {stage, carRoot, frame, ride, panel, reducedMotion}`; returns `{layout({active,onPhoto}), update(dt,{onPhoto})}`.
     - The shell resets carRoot's position and rotation each frame before `update`.
     - The shell's ghost body lives in carRoot; a component's `ghost: {fill, edge}` controls its opacity (0/0 hides it).
   - **Panel widgets:** readouts, trace, buttons (toggle `[on,off]`, or radio with `pressed`), slider, meter, cells, legend, key, svg, text, list, plus card `badge`.
     - `ctx.panel([...])` can be called again and returns the same API.
     - Widget ids must be unique per component.
     - Handles: `ui.set`, `ui.toggle(id).set`, `ui.slider(id).set`, `ui.meter(id).set(f, hot)`, `ui.cells(id).set(i, text, on)`, `ui.badge(id).set(text, on)`, `ui.el(id)`.
   - **Colours** only via tokens: `stage.bind`, `stage.tokenMat(token, opts)`, `stage.color(token)` (cached THREE.Color), `stage.onTheme(fn)`, `var(--…)` in SVG.
     - Tokens: `--l1` red/orange, `--l2` yellow, `--l3` green, `--l4` blue, `--metal`, `--accent`, `--muted`, `--fg`, `--rule`, `--stage`.
   - **Helpers** (`lib/scene/helpers.js`): `V`, `mm`, `Y`, `mat`, `glass`, `line`, `rod`/`place`, `ball`, `helix`, `tyre(m, R, r)` (axis y), `wireWheel(tyreMat, spokeLineMat(with userData.solid), R, r, spokeR, spokes)`, `spokedWheel`, `edgesOf`, `arc`, `profileExtrude`, `pipe(points, r, m)`, `gear(R, teeth, w, m)` (axis x), `polyline`/`at`, `particles(n, size)` → `{pts, set(i,p,c), flush()}`.
   - **Frame conventions:**
     - The stage has no ground.
     - Each car's z origin is set by its subsystem convention (victoria: ground z = 0; road.js: axle z = 0).
     - New cars use ground z = 0, documented in each car.js header.
   - **Service worker** cache-first, stamped by `tools/build.mjs`. CI runs tests and then deploys Pages.
   - The caveman hook may elide Read output; use `sed -n` / `awk` via Bash.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **`lib/model/differential.js`** (new)
   - `cornerSpeeds({halfTrack, wheelR}, radius, v)` → `{left, right, carrier, diff}`, with radius + = left and Infinity = straight.
   - `traction({torque, wheelR, normal, muL, muR, locked, resist})` → `{fL, fR, total, spinL, spinR, moves}`.
     - Open: `each = min(want/2, gripL, gripR)`; `spinL = want/2 > gripL && gripL <= gripR` (and symmetric for the right).
     - Locked: force split proportional to grip.

   **`lib/model/gearbox.js`** (rewritten as a two-shaft sliding-gear box)
   ```js
   export function ratio(box, g) { const s = box.gears[g]; return s ? (s.idler ? -1 : 1) * s.driven / s.drive : Infinity; }
   export const roadSpeed = (box, g, rpm) => (Number.isFinite(ratio(box, g)) ? rpm / ratio(box, g) / box.final * 2 * Math.PI * box.wheelR * 0.06 : 0);
   export const primaryRpmFor = (box, g, kmh) => kmh / 0.06 / (2 * Math.PI * box.wheelR) * box.final * ratio(box, g);
   export function mismatch(box, g, primaryRpm, kmh) { const a = primaryRpm, b = primaryRpmFor(box, g, kmh), top = Math.max(Math.abs(a), Math.abs(b)); return top < 15 ? 0 : Math.abs(a - b) / top; }
   ```

   **`lib/model/aero.js`** (new; RHO 1.2)
   - Exports: `drag`, `rolling`, `powerNeeded` (÷ eta, default 0.88), `topSpeed` (bisection 0–200 m/s), `accelerate(c, P, v, dt)` (grip cap `c.grip ?? 0.5mg`).

   **`lib/model/truss.js`** (new; mm and N)
   - `solveTruss` uses `gauss` from linkage.js and auto-holds nodes no member touches.
   - `tubeFrame(stations, bays, EA)` → `{nodes, members (with tag), node(s, side, level)}`.
     - Each station has 6 nodes; ring members per station.
     - A station's top-level ring is built only if an adjacent bay is not `door: "low"`.
     - Bays: `door: "low"` drops the top longitudinal and the upper side diagonal; `top: true` adds a top diagonal.
   - `twistTest(frame, front, rear, F)`: supports are rear-left floor xyz, rear-right floor xz and front-right floor z; the load goes upward at the front-left floor. Returns `twist` (deg) and `stiffness` (N·m/deg).
   - Calibration with stations z = [floor, sill 260, top] gives a high/low ratio of 2.9×.

   **`lib/model/crash.js`** (new)
   - `crushForce(zone, cellK, x)` and `simulateCrash({mass, v0, zone, cellK}, dt=2e-5)` → `{t, x, a(g) every 1 ms, peakG, meanG, crush, intrusion, duration}`.
   - Zone types: `{type:"crumple", force, length, ramp}` and `{type:"stiff", k, length}`.
   - Calibration at 50 km/h, 1300 kg:
     - crumple {260e3, 0.55, 0.06}, cellK 8e6: peak 20.4 g, crush 0.512, no intrusion, 72 ms;
     - stiff {k 2.6e6, length 0.3}, cellK 2.5e6: peak 63 g, intrusion 11 mm, 35 ms.

   **`lib/model/air-spring.js`** (new)
   - `airStatic(a, mass)` → `{pg, k, f}`; `steelStatic(k, mass, emptyMass)`.
   - `createCorner({kind, air, k, emptyMass, damping, valveRate = 0.15, tol = 0.002, full = 0.02})`.
     - The valve is proportional: `s.C *= 1 + valveRate * clamp(z/full) * dt` outside ±tol.
     - Methods: `step(mass, dt)`, `pressure()` (gauge, Pa).
   - Calibration: air {area 0.012, volume 0.003, n 1.3}, corner 420 → 560 kg: 3.43 → 4.58 bar, 1.29 → 1.26 Hz. Steel at 28 kN/m sags 49 mm.

   **`lib/model/wankel.js`** (new; m)
   - Exports: `housing(alpha, g)`, `rotorCentre`, `apexAngle(θ, k) = θ/3 + 2πk/3`, `apexes`, `displacement = 3√3·e·R·b`, `flank(θ, k, g, n)` (circular arc, sagitta `g.flank`), `chamberOutline`, `chamberVolume`, `compressionRatio(g)`.
   - Stroke classification:
   ```js
   export const STROKES = ["Intake", "Compression", "Power", "Exhaust"];
   export function strokeOf(theta, k) {
     const q = (((apexAngle(theta, k) + Math.PI / 3 - Math.PI / 2) / (Math.PI / 2)) % 4 + 4) % 4;
     return { stroke: STROKES[Math.floor(q)], f: q % 1 };
   }
   ```
   - Ports are on +y and plugs at the −y waist. Chamber 0: intake 90–360°, compression 360–630°, power 630–900°, exhaust 900–1170°. Chamber k runs 360° ahead of chamber k−1.
   - M 950 F: e 15, R 99, b 75 mm (Wikipedia), flank 16.9 mm (illustrative) → compression ≈ 9.3, swept 578 cc, minimum gap about 1.6 mm.

   **`lib/model/cooling.js`** (new)
   - `uaAt(p, v)` (still + (1−still)·√min(v/ref, 2)), `steadyTemp`, `boilRate(p, heat, v)` (kg/s), `perHundredKm(rate, kmh)` (Infinity when kmh ≤ 0.5), `createCooling(p)` → `{T, boiled, q, boiling, step(heat, v, dt), reset()}`.
   - Calibration:
     - tubular {water 20, ua 70, refSpeed 30 km/h, still 0.15, airT 20} at 9 kW and 30 km/h → 18 l/100 km;
     - honeycomb {ua 445, refSpeed 60, still 0.3} at 39 kW and 60 km/h → 9 l/100 km.

   **`lib/model/engine.js`** (edited)
   - Added `TIMING.diesel: [4π − 0.35, 0.1]`.
   - Added `export const injectingDiesel = ph => ph > TIMING.diesel[0] || ph < TIMING.diesel[1];`.
   - Added `export const compressionTemp = (ratio, t1 = 20, n = 1.3) => (t1 + 273.15) * ratio ** (n - 1) - 273.15;`.

   **`subsystems/inline-engine.js`** (edited; was already modified before this session)
   - The root group sits at the crank centre: `root.position.set(xc, 0, crankZ)`, `root.rotation.set(...p.rot deg)`, and `group` is offset back. `layout` toggles `root.visible`.
   - `flywheelR` param; the plain flywheel is now a spinning group with a mark, pushed to `flywheels`.
   - `valvetrain "none"` → `c.valves = []`.
   - `"ohv"`:
     - `camLow = x => at(x, r + 0.09, -1.9 * bR)` and `pushDx`;
     - a low camshaft rod plus timing rod;
     - per valve, `v.push` and `v.rocker`, with the pushrod rising and the rocker going to the valve tip;
     - lobes positioned at `camLow`.
   - `fuel "prechamber"`: `c.pre` ball at `at(x, deck + 0.42bR)`, an injector rod, and a spray cone visible on `injectingDiesel`. The prechamber colour turns `--l1` when flash > 0.15.
   - `p.compression {value, min, max}` adds a "Why no spark plug" card:
     - slider `crs`;
     - readouts `cr`, `hot`, `ign` (250 °C, illustrative);
     - badge `ignites`;
     - text about 6:1 petrol ratios and glow plugs.
   - Header comment updated with the new options.

   **Test files (new)**
   - **`tests/unit/drivetrain.test.mjs`:**
     - Differential corner and traction (with a dry case at torque 2000 and an equal-grip "both spin" case).
     - Gearbox ratios, inverse functions and mismatch.
     - Aero balance; doubling power gives a ratio between ∛2 and 1.35.
     - The run never exceeds top speed.
     - Every aero config's `params.shapes[]` with `quoted` must match `topSpeed(s, s.ps*735.5)` within 5 %.
   - **`tests/unit/body.test.mjs`:**
     - Truss single bar and a 3-4-5 triangle (forces −3750 and +2250).
     - Every `space-frame` config: high stiffness > 2 × low, using `params.stations`, `params.bays` (door bays marked `door`) and `params.EA`. **Currently failing only because no config exists yet.**
     - Crash energy check; stiff vs crumple.
     - Every `crumple-zone` config: `cases[0]` has no intrusion, while `cases[1]` has intrusion and a higher peak at `params.speed.value`.
     - Air-spring static and dynamic checks.
   - **`tests/unit/engines2.test.mjs`:**
     - Wankel apexes, swept volume, flank inside the housing, strokes, chamber offsets (`d*D - k*2π`), compression ≈ 9.3.
     - Every `wankel` config: `params.geometry` in mm and `params.compression`.
     - Cooling calibration and dynamics.
     - Diesel: `compressionTemp(20.5) > 400`, `compressionTemp(6) < 250`, injection window.
   - Unit status: 61 tests, 60 pass; only the space-frame config test fails.

   **`subsystems/differential.js`** (new)
   - Params: `label`, `mode "corner"|"grip"`, `halfTrack`, `wheelR`, `axleX`, `wheel "wire"|"tyre"`, `tyreW`, `ringR`, `drive "crown"|"belt"`, `counter? {x, z, half}`, `corner? {kmh, minRadius}`, `grip? {torque, normal, muLow, muHigh, resist, surface, locks}`.
   - `K = counter ? 0.22/0.07 : 1` (half-shaft turns per wheel turn). `angL`/`angR` are half-shaft angles; wheel rotation = ang/K. Chain sprockets are ordered [left small, left big, right small, right big].
   - Spiders rotate at `(angL − angC) * 16/10`, opposite signs.
   - Corner mode:
     - slider `curve` (auto sin(0.35t));
     - readouts `radius`, `left`, `right`, `spider`, `extra`;
     - wheel path lines.
   - Grip mode:
     - buttons `open`/`lock`, with auto toggling the lock every 5 s if `locks`;
     - readouts `fL`, `fR`, `total`, `spin`;
     - badge `moves`;
     - a blue patch under the left wheel.
   - `[wL, wR] = locked ? [wC, wC] : r.spinL ? [2wC, 0] : r.moves ? [wC, wC] : [0, 0]`.

   **`subsystems/gearbox.js`** (new)
   - Params: `label`, `box`, `module`, `pos [x, z]`, `pitch`, `width`, `rpm {idle, max}`, `gate [[name, col, row]]`, `drive {accel, roll, drag}`.
   - Primary shaft on top, secondary below; one pair per gear (the reverse pair at 0.8× with an idler); the primary gear or idler slides by `w*1.3`.
   - Pair colours: `--l1` in mesh, `--l2` grinding, `--metal` apart.
   - State: `kmh`, `eng`, `prim`, `sel`, `want`, `clutchIn`, `braking`, `throttle`. TOL 0.1; a pending gear engages once `mismatch < TOL`.
   - Physics in 4 substeps. In gear with the clutch up, `eng = max(|need|, idle*1.3)` and `prim = need`.
   - Panel:
     - badge `mesh`; SVG gate with knob;
     - buttons `g0..gN` plus `gn`, `clutch`, `brake`;
     - slider `thr`;
     - readouts `kmh`, `eng`, `prim`, `need`;

   - The demo script shifts 1→4, holds 4th for 6 s, then brakes to a stop and loops. `show(dt)` updates the visuals. Secondary rpm = `kmh/0.06/(2π·wheelR)·final`.

   **`subsystems/radiator.js`** (new)
   - Params: `label`, `heat`, `airT`, `speed`, `types [{id, label, kind "tank"|"tubular"|"honeycomb", ua, still, refSpeed (km/h), water, fan?}]`, `engine {x, z, l, w, h}`, `radiator {x, z, w, h, d}`.

   - Panel:

   **`subsystems/aero.js`** (new)

   - Calibrations:

     - Streamliner {0.36, 2.3, 2500, 0.02, 0.70, 180 PS} → 184.8;
     - Cabriolet {0.48, same} → 169.6.

   **`subsystems/space-frame.js`** (new)
   - Params: `label`, `stations`, `bays`, `EA`, `load`, `exaggerate`, `modes {high, low}` labels.

- **Older name:** Collection 4 was once called the "Gallery of Names." A 2017 report says the room presents vehicles of famous individuals, such as Pope John Paul II., Lady Diana, Emperor Wilhelm II and Konrad Adenauer.

content.text:
The ten new cars are in, and the route now has 16 stops. All 71 unit tests and all 73 e2e tests pass. I loaded every new stop in WebKit with no errors and checked a screenshot of each mechanism. Nothing is committed yet.

| Level · room | Stop | What you can play with |
|---|---|---|
| 8 · Legend 1 | Benz Patent-Motorwagen 1886 | Engine lying flat with a horizontal flywheel; a differential on a countershaft, driven by belt and chains |
| 8 · Legend 1 | Daimler business vehicle 1899 | Maybach's tubular radiator against a plain water tank |
| 7 · Legend 2 | Mercedes-Simplex 1902 | A gearbox without synchromesh that grinds if the speeds don't match; honeycomb against tubular radiator |
| 7 · Legend 2 | Blitzen-Benz 1909 | The 21.5-litre four with pushrod valves; a record run (the model reaches 228 km/h) |
| 6 · Legend 3 | 260 D 1936 | Diesel prechamber injection; a compression slider that shows when the fuel lights by itself |
| 6 · Legend 3 | 540 K (existing stop) | New "Air drag" component: Streamliner (185 km/h) against Cabriolet (170 km/h) |
| 5 · Legend 4 | 300 SL 1954 | Twisting the tube frame, deep sides against cut down for doors (about 3× softer); straight-six laid over 45° with direct injection |
| 4 · Legend 5 | 220 S 1959 | Slow-motion wall crash: crumple zone at about 21 g with the cell intact, against a stiff front at about 62 g that pushes into the cell |
| 4 · Legend 5 | 300 SEL 6.3 1968 | Load the car: air springs level back up and keep the same ride frequency; steel springs stay sunk |
| 4 · Legend 5 | C 111-II 1970 | Four-rotor Wankel engine with an end view colouring the three chambers by stroke |
| 4 · Collection 4 | 230 G Popemobile 1980 | One wheel on ice: with the open differential the car is stuck; with the lock it pulls away |

**Code**
- There are eight new mechanisms. Each has a model with unit tests, and each subsystem file explains its parameters in its header.
- I changed two existing files. The engine subsystem now supports pushrod valves, diesel and a flat engine. The aero subsystem has an optional `ground` setting so the 540 K's road sits at the right height.

**Accuracy**
- **Illustrative values:** each page lists its own in the "unverified" box. Gear teeth, drag values other than the 540 K's measured Cd 0.36, crash forces, spring rates and frame tubes are all illustrative.
- **Not yet sourced:** three facts are now listed under Open in CLAUDE.md.
  - the 260 D's 20.5 : 1 compression ratio;
  - the Simplex's gear count and ratios;
  - the Blitzen-Benz's valve gear.
- **Popemobile room:** Mercedes-Benz's media kit puts the Popemobile in Collection 4, the Gallery of Celebrities. The level (4) is my guess.
- **To confirm at the museum:** rooms and levels, and whether the 220 S is in Legend 4 or 5.

Shall I commit this, and push to deploy?

Sources:
- [Mercedes-Benz Museum media information](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/content/dam/brandhub/assets/art-and-culture/mercedes-benz-museum/museum/Media-Information-Mercedes-Benz-Museum-EN.pdf)
- [Wikipedia: Mercedes-Benz OM 138](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_OM_138)
- [Wikipedia: Mercedes-Benz 260 D](https://wikipedia.com/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_260_D)
- [ingenieur.de: Mercedes 260 D](https://www.ingenieur.de/technik/fachbereiche/verkehr/mercedes-260-d-der-erste-dieselmotor-in-einem-serien-pkw/)
- [CarAdvice: 1936 Mercedes-Benz 260 D](https://www.caradvice.com.au/news/1936-mercedes-benz-260-d/)
- [emercedesbenz: Mercedes-Benz Museum](https://emercedesbenz.com/autos/mercedes-benz/classic/mercedes-benz-museum-offers-a-one-of-a-kind-look-at-automotive-history)
- [MB Heritage: Gallery of Names](https://mercedesheritage.com/?p=4200)
yes, commit and push and deploy
